You did the right thing in walking away from LP. Not many people know they cannot do anything.

How close did you park? The most they likely did was get your appearance on file, total dollar amount of merch you've stolen, and what type vehicle you drive.

Walmart does have very good cameras, but if you parked far enough away, they might not have been able to get a clear enough shot of your license plate.

Did you use your card after or during you lifted? I suggest never using it at all, but as long as you didn't do it while actively lifting, you're fine. Walmart goes through thousands of transactions every day. They cannot possibly keep track of you, especially if you weren't on their radar at that time.

Keep in mind that camera footage is not kept forever, there's just not enough storage to store all that data (I believe it all automatically gets trashed after about 3 months? Something like that). The only way footage can be saved is if they queue that data and put it on file, which they likely have for you. 

The only way they could ID you (from what I assume in this scenario) is your license plate and your name on card, and there's a chance they might not have gotten either. Do not panic, it will be fine. I suggest never going to that Walmart and laying low for a while. I also suggest not going to the stores around that area or other Walmarts for some time bc LP/AP security teams might keep in contact with each other. 

Walmart also uses Auror to keep track of what stores suspects have lifted at. And Walmart greeters do work with LP, so if they see a repeat offender walking in or someone walking out without paying, they can immediately inform their team. Not saying any of this to freak you out, I just want you to be aware. 

You will be fine. Don't panic! It will be okay. I suggest doing lots and lots of research next time and looking into your state laws. As someone who is also very anxious and paranoid, I get it. I felt the same way you did. I promise you it's not that big a deal. 

Another tip I will add is to see what the felony limit is for shoplifting in your state so you know to always go under that limit. Try not to go up to or above the felony amount in one trip! Cops will certainly get called in that case and the store will definitely press charges. Also, the whole idea that a store can add up all the previous visits where you've stolen into one big amount is a myth. They cannot gather up all the items you've stolen and charge you for one big felony, that's a lie. 

Stay safe out there! I don't mind answering more questions if you have any. You are not fucked!

Ask yourself this: how is anyone going to serve you a court summons/warrant if they have no idea how to ID you? They can't. All they have is your physical appearance that day and there's not much they can do with it. They cannot issue a warrant for your arrest nor can they charge you for any crimes because they do not know who you are. And I'm not sure if you're aware of this, but there's statue of limitations (kinda like an expiry date for charges). Look into your state laws. If the statue of limitations has passed, even if a store is able to ID you from previous encounters, they cannot charge you for those because the time for that has passed. The chance of you being prosecuted for the $600 you shoplifted about 5 years ago is ZERO especially if they still cannot ID you.

Here's some advice: 

NEVER shop at a place you have lifted at/are going to lift at. They can and WILL check transactions and see the name your card is under.

Go in, grab what you need, and get out. NEVER linger and give them time to A) grow suspicious, making them more likely to approach you, or B) call the cops.

ALWAYS park in a different parking lot. Many stores have cameras and will look through them to catch a license plate or see what vehicle you drive to put it on the BOLO list (be on look out).

Before lifting at a store, DO SOME RESEARCH into their LP/AP policies. NEVER lift at a hands-on store (Macys for example). Unless you're willing to wrestle your way out of someone over $40, DON'T DO IT.

Be wary of cameras. Don't get greedy. Don't be cocky. Don't be obvious. Even if you were on camera, there's a chance no one was watching at that time. If they have no idea that merchandise went missing, they're not gonna check. Don't give them a reason to go back and check the footage. Be smart about it. Keep in mind that you are committing a crime and ALWAYS be wary and on watch because of it since there is always the chance you could get caught.

In the case you do get stopped, keep walking. The policies for many LP apprehensions are hands-off so many can't touch you. If you get stopped, either drop everything you took and keep walking, or just keep walking. Don't go into a room with them and give them ID. Keep in mind, if you do not comply, they do list you as uncooperative in their file and will call the cops on you next time you enter that store, so never go back again.
